finding.trigger: Two otherwise valid saved camera records share an ID, e.g. generated Front and Back rows with id 42 and distinct rtsp://*.local/live URLs. Load returns both IDs unchanged; removing one ID filters both records.

historyEvidence.fact: Original add saved Camera(System.currentTimeMillis(),...), so same-millisecond rapid adds could create duplicate IDs; current new-add uniqueness prevents only new collisions.

finding.userImpact: Confirming removal of one legacy camera silently removes all cameras with its ID; selecting a later duplicate opens the first saved stream. No invented security/audio/media claim.
finding.existingTests: CameraConfigTest covers ordinary append, exact removal with distinct IDs, concurrent new add/remove uniqueness; no legacy duplicate-ID or missing-ID stability case.
finding.minimalSafeReproduction: Generated in-memory SharedPreferences array with two valid same-ID rows. Actual CameraConfig.load then removeAndLoad(selected second ID) should preserve first row; original deletes both. Independently show load(...).firstOrNull{id==selected.id} resolves wrong row. No real URL connection or owner preferences required.

findings: Two optLong defaults retain existing JSON coercion while distinguishing missing/unconvertible IDs from real Long.MIN_VALUE.
All converted IDs of retained nonblank-URL rows are reserved before allocation; first occurrence retains ID, later duplicates and missing IDs receive deterministic unique replacements.
The deterministic snapshot is stable on repeated loads, with no new preference writes. Existing synchronized mutations persist the normalized list under the same config monitor.
Existing viewer/Tools callers and UI geometry are unchanged; names, URL strings, order and already-unique IDs are preserved.
review.scope: Actual debug and optimized APK CameraConfig load/Add/Remove with Android JSON and generated in-memory preferences. Selected-camera lookup is caller-equivalent ID lookup, not actual Viewer/UI/RTSP. No owner preference writes, network/camera/player/credential use, all-firmware acceptance, concurrent raw restore/ABA or already-open old Intent migration guarantee; no injected timeout cleanup proof.

limits: Native acceptance invokes actual APK CameraConfig with generated process-local preferences and Android JSON. ID lookup mirrors the existing caller; CameraViewerActivity, VideoView, RTSP, camera connectivity, routing and UI acceptance were not exercised.

Owner camera URLs and credentials are not used by the fixture. Complete camera preference bytes, alongside the other captured room maps and preference files, remain unchanged across local delivery.
